steps.text: **The question of this lesson.** On move five Black can invite the Alien Gambit or avoid it. By the end you can compare the five main replies with engine and game data, say when the knight sacrifice on f7 works and when it fails, and check a claim before you trust it. Marks: [V] checked here, [S] one source, [R] recalled, [I] inference, [H] guess.

steps.text: **When does the sacrifice work?** The knight on f7 forks the queen and a rook, but the king can take it. The king taking is the first thing to check: if it can, the sacrifice just loses a piece. If it cannot, also check that the knight on f7 still forks something worth winning. Look at the original position, then change one thing and predict. Two tested positions are not a law [I].

steps.text: **How to check a claim [I].** A claim is a sentence about a position and a move, such as 'after ...c5 the knight sacrifice wins'. Check it in three steps. One: write the claim down, with its position and move. Two: open the Analysis page, set up the position and play the claimed move. Three: read the engine line and say whether the claim held. Two claims are checked below; then you test one.

If f7 is defended or the king has left, check the knight still forks something worth winning.'

steps.text: **Recap.** Five replies are within half a pawn of level (engine, depth 20) [V]. ...h6 invites the sacrifice; the other four decline it. Check first whether the king can take on f7: if it can, the sacrifice just loses a piece [V]. If it cannot, also check that the knight still forks the queen or a rook.
